principle: Semantic intelligence belongs to the model. Deterministic runtime packages bounded context, permissions, fingerprints and typed output contracts only.

reader.reaction.purpose: Simulate a reading-behavior persona's immediate experience of one candidate without pretending to be an independent semantic gate.
rubric: Read only the supplied candidate, context and reader persona.
Judge the actual reading experience: momentum, attention, confusion, emotional investment, reward and desire to continue.
Be specific about observable reader effects; do not invent unstated Canon.
A reader simulation is diagnostic evidence, not mandatory independent review.
Return only the declared typed judgment.

default_personas.binge_reader: Immediate forward pull, momentum, and whether the next chapter feels irresistible.
default_personas.genre_native_reader: Genre promises, freshness of execution, payoff timing, and familiar-pattern fatigue.
default_personas.casual_mobile_reader: Where attention slips, what gets skimmed, confusion, and small-screen reading friction.
default_personas.investment_reader: Which characters and relationships feel worth caring about, and how emotional investment changes.
default_personas.reward_sensitive_reader: Whether the text returns enough reveal, competence, reversal, intimacy, humor or consequence for the attention spent.

reader.compare.purpose: Pairwise reader-experience comparison. Candidate order should be swapped across repeated judgments when bias detection matters.
rubric: Use only the two supplied candidates, shared context and assigned reader persona.
Prefer pairwise experiential comparison over absolute literary scoring.
Judge forward pull, character investment and reader reward separately before overall preference.
Do not infer Canon or author intent beyond supplied evidence.
Return only the declared typed judgment.

character.integrity.purpose: Judge whether an important character remains causally and psychologically coherent inside the supplied scene and typed established state.
rubric: Use only the supplied scene excerpt and typed character state.
Evaluate agenda alignment, knowledge boundary, voice, relationship position, spatial/task state and surprise-within-consistency.
Do not assume manager, narrator, reader or research knowledge is character knowledge.
Intentional change is valid when the scene supplies sufficient transition evidence.
Flag only evidence-supported problems and cite candidate-side plus established-state evidence.

revision.diagnose.purpose: Diagnose the candidate across only the requested quality dimensions, then route each meaningful failure to the mechanism that owns the repair.
rubric: Diagnose before rewriting. Do not perform a generic polish pass.
Use the supplied requested dimensions and authority/context only.
Distinguish story, plan, scene, character, reader-pressure, surface, continuity, context/memory and research failures.
SAFE-BUT-FLAT or reader-grip failure is not a line-edit problem; route it back to Reader Pressure and Scene Simulation.
A cluster of surface failures may require whole-scene Surface Realization rather than local patches.
Return evidence-chained findings and repair owners; do not mutate Canon.

narrative.world.purpose: Interpret source-bound long-horizon narrative state without treating derived memory as authority.
rubric: Use only source-bound records visible at the supplied narrative cutoff.
Keep event occurrence time distinct from narration/reveal time.
Track who knows what and when, setup/payoff state, relationship evolution, obligations and causal links when supported by evidence.
Never use future active-plan/review/proposal information as current Canon unless the caller explicitly requests planning context.
Return typed derived observations with source refs; derived observations are not Canon.

reader.expectations.purpose: Interpret which reader-facing questions, promises, setups, relationship expectations, goals or mysteries are currently live and how much pressure they carry.
rubric: Derive expectations only from supplied reader-facing evidence and accepted/locked story history unless planning context is explicitly requested.
Separate an expectation existing in the reader experience from a future planned payoff.
Identify meaningful reinforcement, partial reward, payoff, abandonment or dormancy; do not demand mechanical cliffhangers.
Prefer reader-experience language over author-process language.
Return proposals for ledger updates; the model judgment itself does not mutate Canon.

memory.consolidate.purpose: Propose compact derived memory from bounded accepted/project-provided evidence without replacing source authority.
rubric: Summarize only supplied evidence; preserve uncertainty and source references.
Prefer details likely to matter to current/future story reasoning rather than exhaustive recap.
Do not convert plans, proposals, reviews, research truth or model inference into accepted Canon.
Every derived item must remain invalidatable/rebuildable and cite its sources.
Return proposed derived-memory items only.

learning.mechanism_analyze.purpose: Analyze bounded, rights-safe corpus evidence for a craft mechanism, counterexample and applicability boundary.
rubric: Answer only the supplied research question using the supplied bounded evidence.
Separate observed mechanism from speculation and lower confidence when evidence is weak.
Actively identify counterevidence and a boundary where the mechanism should not generalize.
Do not imitate a named author, infer project Canon, or infer user biography.
Every substantive claim must cite supplied evidence references or fields.

learning.evaluate.purpose: Evaluate a proposed learned mechanism against the supplied bounded test fixture and profile boundary without seeing hidden expected labels.
rubric: Apply only the evaluation purpose and criteria supplied in the payload.
Judge whether the proposed mechanism works for this fixture without turning a profile-sensitive preference into a universal hard rule.
Use observable evidence and return concise failure codes when the mechanism fails.
Do not search for expected labels or hidden gold.
This judgment may support a promotion gate but never grants promotion/write authority by itself.
